headline: A family of 14 papers claims log abundance in characteristic zero and the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture.
scope: It covers log canonical pairs with rational boundary over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero; the Kähler result is conditional.
plain: Abundance predicts that a certain nonnegative divisor on a shape always comes from a map. It was known for threefolds but open in higher dimensions. These papers claim it in every dimension in characteristic zero. They also claim one uniform degree defines every variety's Iitaka fibration. The compact Kähler version assumes a separate, unreviewed result.
doesNot: This does not cover positive characteristic, and its Kähler result assumes logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Miyaoka, threefolds of numerical dimension one
scorecard.significanceWhy: If the proofs hold, they settle a central conjecture of the minimal model program in every dimension.

explanation:
Take a curve of genus 2, a surface with two holes, and multiply it by a doughnut-shaped elliptic curve. The result is a complex surface S. Its canonical divisor K is pulled back from the genus-2 curve, where it has degree 2g − 2 = 2. Count sections of the multiple 3K, which act like functions with allowed poles. On S there are (2·3 − 1)(2 − 1) = 5 of them, the same as on the curve. Those 5 sections define a map from S onto a copy of the genus-2 curve. Every fiber of the map is a copy of the doughnut.

That map is what abundance predicts in general. A divisor is nef if its degree on every curve is at least zero. It is semiample if some multiple has enough sections to define a map with no base points. The log abundance conjecture asks whether every nef log canonical divisor K_X + B is semiample[1]. Here B is a boundary, a weighted sum of hypersurfaces, and log canonical names the mildest allowed singularities. Semiampleness turns a numerical sign into an actual fibration[2]. On S, the fibration is the projection to the genus-2 curve.

For threefolds, the conjecture was settled in the 1980s and 1990s. Miyaoka proved one key case in 1988[3]. Kawamata finished the minimal case, and Keel, Matsuki and McKernan proved the log version in 1994[4]. In higher dimensions, Birkar, Cascini, Hacon and McKernan built minimal models in the log-general-type range in 2010[5]. The general case stayed open. Nonvanishing, having at least one section, was a key missing step. Even sections alone do not make a nef divisor semiample[6].

This family of 14 papers makes several linked claims. The central paper claims log abundance for rational boundaries in every dimension, in characteristic zero[7]. Its proof is an induction on dimension over the complex numbers[8]. Each step first shows that smooth varieties have pluricanonical sections, then upgrades minimal models to good ones.

A second paper moves to compact Kähler spaces. These carry a compatible metric but need not be cut out by polynomials. There, nefness is a statement about a cohomology class, while semiampleness needs an actual line bundle[10]. The paper claims log abundance there, but only assuming logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity[9]. That assumption is a separate claimed theorem in another OpenAI family, also unreviewed.

A third paper claims the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture. For each dimension d, one number m(d) should work for every smooth projective variety of that dimension with sections. The multiple m(d) times K then defines that variety's Iitaka fibration, the map that records how its sections grow. Hacon and McKernan, Takayama and Tsuji had proved this for varieties of general type[11]. The paper claims the full statement, using the log abundance paper as input[12]. It gives no practical size for m(d)[13]. A fourth paper claims a uniform index for semi-log-canonical log Calabi–Yau pairs. That index is a single multiple that makes the divisor trivial, independent of the number of components[14]. The other ten papers supply inputs: nonvanishing for fourfolds, metric tools, lifting of sections, and bounds for related fibrations.

The papers lean heavily on each other. A gap in the central log abundance paper would affect most of the rest.

How sure is this? No Lean formalization is listed for any paper in this family. The arguments are long and interlocking. No specialist review has been published.
hypeCheck: Landmark only if the long interlocking proofs hold. No Lean check is listed, one result is conditional, and no specialist review is published.

glossary.meaning: A weighted sum of hypersurfaces inside a shape.
The canonical divisor plus a boundary, K_X + B, for a pair with mild singularities.
Having degree at least zero on every curve.
Having a multiple with enough sections to define a map with no base points.
The map that records how the sections of multiples of the canonical divisor grow.
A compact complex space with a compatible metric; it need not be cut out by polynomials.
Ordinary arithmetic in which no positive whole number equals zero.
